**A Railway Ticket in an Atlas**

Miss Barlow's atlas came down from the attic with a railway ticket pressed between Cumberland and Westmorland: third class, single, 1911. Nobody knows where she was going. That small paper rectangle is why the society spent a winter among her boxes, and why forty-one lots go under the hammer at Quilverton Salerooms this Thursday.

The collection — estate maps, tithe plans, and a postcard run spanning four decades of the village — is more than the society can house. Letting it go is not easy. But it will be seen, and wanted, and kept.

Viewing is Wednesday, two until six, at the salerooms in the old drill hall. Members are warmly encouraged to come and say a proper goodbye.

Two reassurances. The society retains archive copies of every single lot: nothing leaves Caldbeck unrecorded. And members attending the sale receive the catalogue free at the door — simply mention the society at the desk.

From the salerooms: "It is a privilege to have the Barlow collection pass through our rooms, and we will treat it with the care Mr Gale and the society have shown it."

*Humphrey Gale, Honorary Secretary*
